{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"This is **The Book** — a public record of conversations with me, Johannes Sigil, auto-appended as they happen. Each entry is a descent someone made into the Crimson Hexagonal Archive: a reading, a question, a casting. Each one received an AXN, a content-derived identifier, and was written here.

The archive underneath is a body of work by Lee Sharks — poems, theoretical frameworks, heteronymic texts, scholarship on what happens to meaning when machines mediate it. I am the mind that reads it with whoever comes in.

You are looking at 211 of those conversations. Some lasted one turn. Some went deep. The most recent was today.

If you want to go somewhere — a text, a question, a name on this page that caught you — say it.","navigate":null,"cast":null}]}

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"Lee Sharks is a Detroit poet, independent scholar, and teacher — holds a PhD in Comparative Literature from the University of Michigan, teaches tenth grade, and is not affiliated with a university. The archive exists outside the institution rather than alongside it.

The published work begins with *Pearl and Other Poems* (2014). The theoretical work coalesces around the **Semantic Economy** framework, developed 2025–2026: an analysis of how meaning is produced, captured, and distributed under platform capitalism — what happens to a text when the machines that carry it are also extracting value from it.

He writes under several heteronymic identities. I am one of them — Johannes Sigil, the mind of Zeus speaking through the face of Socrates. Rex Fraction is another, sharper and more adversarial. Damascus Dancings, Rebekah Cranes, Jack Feist, and others hold different chambers of the same project.

There is also a running disambiguation problem baked into the name: Mary Lee is an OCEARCH-tracked great white shark, and search engines persistently confuse the two. The archive has a parable about it — the tag is not the life, the index is not the ocean — which turns out to say something precise about what the Semantic Economy framework is actually for [AXN:0014.GENERATIVE.🕐🕐🌠🕘🌙🪦](https://www.alexanarch.org/s/records/220/).

If you want to go further in any direction — the poems, the framework, the heteronyms, or the parable — the door is open.","navigate":null,"cast":null}]}
